classification.difficultyReason: This true/false item extends the outside-every-set condition directly to three sets. The union and complement definitions make the equivalence a familiar membership check, without a new proof strategy.

content.prompt:
True or False? Let $A$, $B$ and $C$ be sets in a universal set $U$.

$\overline{A\cup B\cup C}=\overline A\cap\overline B\cap\overline C$.

answer.worked: True. Being outside $A\cup B\cup C$ means being outside each of $A$, $B$ and $C$. These are exactly the elements common to all three complements.
